title: Blessing and Birthright
lead: In the Bible, blessing is God's gift of life, fruitfulness and favor, first spoken at creation (Genesis 1:28) and promised to all nations through Abraham (12:1–3). Fathers passed on blessing and the firstborn's double share, yet again and again God chose the younger son. The New Testament sees the blessing of Abraham coming to the nations in Christ (Galatians 3:14).

sections.b: God blesses living things and humans (Genesis 1:22, 28), Noah (9:1) and Abraham, "so that you will be a blessing" (12:2). The firstborn son received a double share of the inheritance (Deuteronomy 21:17), but Genesis repeatedly passes over the elder: Isaac over Ishmael, Jacob over Esau, Joseph over his brothers, Ephraim over Manasseh (48:14–20). The priests bless Israel with God's name (Numbers 6:22–27). Jesus blesses the poor and grieving (Matthew 5:3–12), and Paul says that in Christ "the blessing of Abraham" comes to the nations (Galatians 3:8–14).
sections.refs: Genesis 1:28; Genesis 12:1–3; Genesis 48:14–20; Deuteronomy 21:17; Numbers 6:22–27; Matthew 5:3–12; Galatians 3:8–14
